rule: Umbrella criterion 4's second half, mechanised by scripts/sole_home_scan.py. Every row excuses one (source, value) pair: a 'coincidence' says the integer is not that shape count at all, a 'forced_restatement' says it is and that R-17, R-19 or R-34 made writing it unavoidable. Since the umbrella's Amendment H of 2026-08-14 the forced rows are criterion 4's ruled CARVE-OUT rather than its open residue: a leaf's own adjudicating receipt may state that leaf's value, on three conditions -- the restatement sits inside an artifact adjudicating that exact leaf, names the leaf by its path, and agrees with the committed receipt or declares what it supersedes. This file is what keeps the carve-out from widening: every row is one site, a row that outlives its site fails, and a site with no row fails.
how_a_row_retires: A forced row retires when its site stops stating a count of a COMMITTED baseline -- because a re-capture superseded the figure, or because the artifact stops adjudicating that leaf. Editing the sources is not available and never was: a superseded oracle receipt is never edited (R-15/R-18 amendment) and a commit body is history. What changed on 2026-08-14 is the reading, not the mechanism: Amendment H rules these sites carved out rather than owed, and the scan's job became holding the carve-out to its three conditions instead of counting a debt.  The deferral-coverage capture of 2026-08-15 did it a fourth time and at the widest reach yet, because it moved every coupled census at once -- both entry counts, both leaf counts and the coupled numeric-leaf count -- so every row still keyed to one of them stopped having a site in the same commit: two commit bodies' R-34 lines, one oracle receipt's numeric-leaf figure, one allowlist's leaf figure now two captures old, and the three coincidences whose integers stopped colliding with a live count the moment the count moved. None is re-keyed and none is edited -- a commit body is history, a superseded oracle receipt is never edited, and an allowlist two captures behind states a figure no reader should be sent to. The residue that remains is the one row whose figure no capture since has superseded.

allowances.reason: R-17: an allowlist states the expected old and new value of every path it claims, and this allowlist claims /metadata/fingerprint/leaves in order to supersede the boundary pin on it, so it cannot make the claim without stating the figure
R-19: an oracle receipt carries the two values of the leaf it adjudicates, and this leaf IS a fingerprint shape counter, so the receipt cannot state the question without stating the figure

a_superseded_count_stops_being_a_site: The charge-price PIN re-capture did it a fourth time, and for the first time in the pair jurisdiction: it is the only capture since the 0B boundary to move golden.leaves and golden.numeric_leaves, so the two rows that stated those two superseded figures -- 1483b46e's, the 0B capture commit's own line of cause under R-34, and oracle-0A.2-golden-leaf0.json's numeric-leaf figure under R-19 -- retired outright, with no re-keying available to either: a commit body is history and a superseded oracle receipt is never edited. The 0A.2 receipt keeps its entry-count row, which that capture did not move. The scan reads the LIVE counts from campaign-fingerprints.json, so a receipt restating a count a later re-capture superseded stops being a site the moment the capture lands -- which is what the criterion says, since it binds a count OF A COMMITTED BASELINE and a superseded figure is no longer one. The campaign-close coupled re-capture moved coupled_golden.leaves and retired six rows that way; the seventh, this file's H2 allowlist, is re-keyed to the new value because an allowlist states both sides of the move it claims. The stale-row check is what makes that visible rather than quiet: a row outliving its site fails. The 2026-08-14 exact-capture move did it again and in both directions: three rows stating the old exact leaf count retired the moment the capture superseded it, and one allowlist's unrelated occurrence count became a collision the same day. Both are recorded rather than reasoned about, which is what the stale-row check is for. The campaign-close BOUNDARY re-capture did it a third time: the H2 allowlist's row retired outright because its stated figure is now two captures old, and the dispositions allowlist's row was re-keyed to the figure that capture made live -- the same two moves, in the same order, for the same reason.
